questions.question: The liquid water present in oceans, lakes and rivers gets converted to the gaseous form in the presence of sunlight in the water cycle. This step is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Evaporation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Evaporation is the process by which water changes from a liquid to a gas or vapor.
 
• In the water cycle, evaporation is driven by the heat energy from the sun.
 
• This process primarily occurs at the surface of bodies of water like oceans, lakes, and rivers.
 
• Evaporation is a crucial step in the water cycle, contributing to the formation of clouds and precipitation.
 
• It helps in regulating temperature and is essential for maintaining the earth's climate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Condensation**

 
 
• Condensation is the process where water vapor becomes liquid.
 
• It occurs when the air is saturated with water vapor and cools down.
 
• This process is responsible for the formation of clouds and dew.
 
 
 
• **Precipitation**
 
 
• Precipitation includes various forms of water, such as rain, sleet, snow, and hail, that fall from the sky.
 
• It is a key component of the water cycle, returning water to the Earth's surface.
 
 
 
• **Melting**
 
 
• Melting is the process by which a solid turns into a liquid due to heat.
 
• In the context of the water cycle, it refers to the melting of ice and snow into liquid water.
 
 
 
• **The Water Cycle**
 
 
• The water cycle is a continuous process by which water circulates throughout the Earth and its atmosphere.
 
• It includes processes like evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, and runoff.
 
• This cycle is vital for sustaining life on Earth.

questions.question: Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on the birth anniversary of which of the following freedom fighters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched by the Government of India on **2nd October 2014**, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• This mission aims to achieve the vision of a **Clean India** by 2nd October 2019.
 
• It seeks to eliminate open defecation and improve solid waste management across the country.
 
• The Swachh Bharat Mission is divided into two sub-missions: **Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) and Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin)**

 
 
• Focuses on rural areas with the aim of eliminating open defecation by constructing toilets.
 
• Promotes hygiene and sanitation practices among rural communities.
 
• Encourages the use of proper waste disposal methods.
 
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban)**
 
 
• Targets urban areas with a focus on solid waste management.
 
• Aims to create clean and sanitized public spaces and streets.
 
• Involves urban local bodies in the implementation of the mission.
 
 
 
• **Key Achievements**
 
 
• As of October 2019, India was declared open defecation free (ODF).
 
• Over 100 million household toilets have been constructed under the mission.
 
• Significant behavioral change towards sanitation and hygiene has been observed among citizens.
 
 
 
• **Financial Allocation**
 
 
• The Government of India allocated substantial funds for the implementation of the mission.
 
• Public-private partnerships and community participation have been crucial for its success.

questions.question: As per Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the highest percentage of Hindu population in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Census of India 2011, Himachal Pradesh has the highest percentage of Hindu population among all Indian states.
 
• Approximately 95.17% of the state's population practices Hinduism.
 
• The state has a total population of about 6.8 million, with the majority being Hindus.
 
• Hinduism is deeply rooted in the culture and traditions of Himachal Pradesh, influencing the state's festivals, rituals, and daily life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Religious Demographics in India**

 
 
• Hinduism is the largest religion in India, with about 79.8% of the population adhering to it.
 
• Other major religions include Islam (14.2%), Christianity (2.3%), and Sikhism (1.7%).
 
 
 
• **Hinduism in Himachal Pradesh**
 
 
• Hinduism in Himachal Pradesh is characterized by the worship of various deities, local gods, and goddesses.
 
• Important Hindu temples in the state include the Jakhoo Temple, Baijnath Temple, and the famous Hidimba Devi Temple.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Influence**
 
 
• Hindu festivals like Diwali, Holi, and Navratri are widely celebrated across Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The state's traditional dances, music, and folklore are often themed around Hindu mythology and legends.
 
 
 
• **Census Data Collection**
 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India.
 
• The census collects comprehensive data on the population, including demographics, religion, and socio-economic status.

questions.question: Bharatanatyam Guru _______ received the Nrithya Seva Ratna award from Indian Fine Arts Akademi, San Diego in 2023.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hema Rajagopalan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hema Rajagopalan is a renowned Bharatanatyam dancer and choreographer.
 
• She received the Nrithya Seva Ratna award from the Indian Fine Arts Akademi, San Diego, in 2023.
 
• Hema Rajagopalan is the founder and artistic director of the Natya Dance Theatre in Chicago.
 
• She has been instrumental in promoting Bharatanatyam in the United States for several decades.
 
• Her contributions to Indian classical dance have been recognized both in India and abroad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork combined with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in Hindu religious themes and mythology.
 
• Bharatanatyam was traditionally performed by Devadasis in temples and courts of southern India.
 
• It has evolved into a widely performed dance form both in India and internationally.
 
 
 
• **Indian Fine Arts Akademi, San Diego**
 
 
• The Indian Fine Arts Akademi, San Diego, is an organization dedicated to promoting Indian classical arts in the United States.
 
• It organizes various cultural events, workshops, and performances to celebrate Indian classical music, dance, and other art forms.
 
• The Akademi aims to provide a platform for artists to showcase their talent and preserve the rich cultural heritage of India.
 
 
 
• **Natya Dance Theatre**
 
 
• Natya Dance Theatre is a premier Bharatanatyam dance company based in Chicago, founded by Hema Rajagopalan.
 
• The theatre is dedicated to promoting and preserving the classical dance form of Bharatanatyam.
 
• It offers classes, workshops, and performances to educate and engage audiences in Indian classical dance.
 
• Natya Dance Theatre has received numerous accolades for its artistic excellence and contributions to the cultural landscape.
 
 
 
• **Nrithya Seva Ratna Award**
 
 
• The Nrithya Seva Ratna award is a prestigious recognition given to individuals for their outstanding contributions to Indian classical dance.
 
• It is awarded by various cultural organizations to honor the dedication and achievements of dancers and choreographers.
 
• Recipients of the award are celebrated for their efforts in preserving and promoting the art form.
 
• The award highlights the significance of dance as a cultural and artistic expression.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India mentions that every Minister and the Attorney-General of India shall have the right to speak in and participate in the proceedings of either House of Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 88**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 88** of the Constitution of India provides that every Minister and the Attorney-General of India shall have the right to speak in and take part in the proceedings of either House of Parliament.
 
• However, they shall not be entitled to vote in the House.
 
• This right is provided irrespective of whether they are a member of either House of Parliament or not.
 
• Article 88 ensures that the executive branch of the government is accountable to the legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Attorney-General of India**

 
 
• The Attorney-General is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India.
 
• They are appointed by the President of India under Article 76 of the Constitution.
 
• The Attorney-General has the right to audience in all courts in India, in the performance of their official duties.
 
 
 
• **Role of Ministers in Parliament**
 
 
• Ministers are responsible for the administration of their respective ministries and departments.
 
• They are accountable to the Parliament and must answer questions and provide information as required.
 
• Ministers play a crucial role in the legislative process, including the introduction and defense of bills.
 
 
 
• **Parliament of India**
 
 
• The Parliament of India is a bicameral legislature, consisting of the President of India and two Houses: the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
 
• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, while the Lok Sabha is elected every five years.
 
• Parliament is responsible for making laws, representing the electorate, and overseeing the executive.

questions.question: The training academy for Indian Police Service officers has been named after:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The training academy for Indian Police Service (IPS) officers is named the **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy**.
 
• It is located in **Hyderabad, Telangana, India**.
 
• The academy was named in honor of **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, who is also known as the "Iron Man of India" for his role in the unification of India.
 
• The academy provides training to IPS officers before they are assigned to their respective cadres.
 
• It is an esteemed institution under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**

 
 
• He played a key role in India's independence movement and served as the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India.
 
• Sardar Patel is remembered for his leadership in integrating over 500 princely states into the Indian Union post-independence.
 
• He was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 1991.
 
 
 
• **Indian Police Service (IPS)**
 
 
• The IPS is one of the three All India Services of the Government of India.
 
• It was formed in 1948, replacing the Indian Imperial Police.
 
• IPS officers are responsible for the enforcement of law and order, crime prevention, and investigation across the country.
 
 
 
• **Training at Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy**
 
 
• The training program includes physical fitness, academic knowledge, law enforcement techniques, and leadership skills.
 
• The duration of the training program is around 46 weeks, which includes both indoor and outdoor training sessions.
 
• IPS probationers also undergo practical training in field conditions as part of their curriculum.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Home Affairs**
 
 
• The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is a ministry of the Government of India, responsible for internal security and domestic policy.
 
• It oversees the Indian Police Service (IPS) and the training academies for the police forces.
 
• The current Minister of Home Affairs is Amit Shah (as of 2023).

questions.question: Who is revered as 'Karnataka Sangeeta Pitamaha'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Purandara Dasa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Purandara Dasa is known as the 'Karnataka Sangeeta Pitamaha' (Father of Karnataka Music).
 
• He was a prolific composer, with hundreds of compositions to his credit, primarily in Kannada and Sanskrit.
 
• Purandara Dasa is credited with structuring the teaching methodology for Carnatic music, including the basic lessons for beginners.
 
• He lived during the 15th century and is one of the most revered saints in the Bhakti movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnatic Music**

 
 
• Carnatic music is a system of music commonly associated with southern India, including the states of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Kerala.
 
• It is one of the two main sub-genres of Indian classical music, the other being Hindustani music, which is prevalent in northern India.
 
• Carnatic music is known for its complex rhythmic and melodic structures, called 'Tala' and 'Raga' respectively.
 
• The compositions in Carnatic music are typically devotional in nature, often addressing Hindu deities.
 
 
 
• **Bhakti Movement**
 
 
• The Bhakti movement was a devotional trend that emerged in medieval India and focused on the worship of a personal god and the expression of love and devotion.
 
• This movement transcended the boundaries of caste and creed, promoting the idea of equality and the universal brotherhood of man.
 
• Prominent figures in the Bhakti movement include saints like Kabir, Mirabai, Tulsidas, and Purandara Dasa.
 
• The Bhakti saints composed numerous devotional songs and poems that are still popular today.
 
 
 
• **Purandara Dasa's Contributions**
 
 
• He introduced the 'Maya Malava Gaula' scale as the basic scale for teaching beginners in Carnatic music.
 
• Purandara Dasa's compositions, known as 'Padas', are sung in various Carnatic music concerts and are considered foundational to the genre.
 
• He composed in simple Kannada, making his works accessible to the common people.
 
• He is also credited with popularizing the practice of 'Haridasa' culture, which involves the singing of devotional songs and spreading the message of Bhakti.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about nutrients are correct?

Statement A: C, H, O, N, P and K are macro nutrients.

Statement B: Fe, Mn, Ni, Co and Mo are micronutrients.

Statement C: Micronutrients are not essential for our body.

options.text: All statements A, B and C

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statements A and B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Macro nutrients** include elements such as Carbon (C), Hydrogen (H), Oxygen (O), Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Potassium (K).
 
• **Micro nutrients** include elements like Iron (Fe), Manganese (Mn), Nickel (Ni), Cobalt (Co), and Molybdenum (Mo).
 
• Both macro and micronutrients are essential for plant growth and human health, though required in different quantities.
 
• Statement C is incorrect because micronutrients, despite being needed in smaller amounts, are essential for various bodily functions and overall health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Macronutrients:** These are nutrients required in larger amounts and include carbohydrates, proteins, and fats, along with elements like C, H, O, N, P, and K.
 
• **Micronutrients:** These are nutrients required in smaller amounts but are crucial for various physiological functions. Examples include vitamins and minerals like Fe, Mn, Ni, Co, and Mo.
 
• **Essential Nutrients:** Both macro and micronutrients are categorized as essential because the body cannot synthesize them in sufficient amounts.
 
• **Role of Micronutrients:** Micronutrients play vital roles in enzyme function, hormone production, and maintaining the immune system.
 
• **Deficiency Impacts:** Deficiency of micronutrients can lead to various health issues, including anemia (iron deficiency), scurvy (vitamin C deficiency), and osteoporosis (calcium deficiency).

questions.question: The campaign 'Ek Tareekh, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath' is associated with which occasion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhi Jayanti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The campaign "Ek Tareekh, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath" is associated with Gandhi Jayanti, which is celebrated on October 2nd every year.
 
• This campaign emphasizes the importance of cleanliness and hygiene as part of the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan initiated by the Indian government.
 
• The initiative encourages citizens to dedicate one hour on the 1st of every month to clean their surroundings, promoting community participation in keeping public spaces clean.
 
• The campaign aligns with the broader goals of the Swachh Bharat Mission, aiming to create a cleaner and healthier India.
 
• Gandhi Jayanti marks the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, who was a strong advocate of cleanliness and sanitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Clean India Mission)**

 
 
• Launched on October 2, 2014, by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• Aims to eliminate open defecation and improve solid waste management across India.
 
• It is India's largest cleanliness drive to date, involving millions of government employees and school students.
 
• The mission includes the construction of toilets, promoting sanitation practices, and ensuring the sustainability of sanitation infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**
 
 
• Born on October 2, 1869, in Porbandar, Gujarat.
 
• Known as the 'Father of the Nation' in India for his role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• Advocated for non-violence (Ahimsa) and civil disobedience as methods for social and political change.
 
• His principles of cleanliness and sanitation were integral parts of his vision for a self-reliant India.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi Jayanti**
 
 
• Observed annually on October 2nd to commemorate the birth of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• It is a national holiday in India, with various events organized to honor his legacy.
 
• The United Nations also celebrates this day as the International Day of Non-Violence.
 
 
 
• **Community Participation in Cleanliness Drives**
 
 
• Essential for the success of cleanliness campaigns like "Ek Tareekh, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath".
 
• Fosters a sense of responsibility and ownership among citizens towards public spaces.
 
• Encourages collective action and promotes social cohesion.

questions.question:
Below are two chemical equations:

Zn (s) + CuSO₄ (aq) → ZnSO₄ (aq) + Cu (s)

Pb (s) + CuCl₂ (aq) → PbCl₂ (aq) + Cu (s)

Why does copper get separated from its compound form in both the cases?

options.text: Zinc and Lead are unstable in element form.
Copper compounds break down under high pressure.
Zinc and Lead are more reactive than Copper.
Copper is more reactive than Zinc and Lead.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc and Lead are more reactive than Copper.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Zinc and Lead are higher in the reactivity series than Copper, making them more reactive elements.
 
• In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal will displace a less reactive metal from its compound.
 
• When Zinc reacts with Copper sulfate (CuSO₄), Zinc displaces Copper because Zinc is more reactive.
 
• Similarly, Lead displaces Copper from Copper chloride (CuCl₂) due to its higher reactivity compared to Copper.
 
• This reactivity series is a fundamental concept in chemistry for predicting the outcomes of displacement reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in order of decreasing reactivity.
 
• It helps in predicting the products of displacement reactions and the reactivity of metals with acids and water.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reactions**
 
 
• These are reactions where a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
 
• They are commonly observed in aqueous solutions of metal salts.
 
 
 
• **Electrochemical Series**
 
 
• It is a series of elements arranged by their standard electrode potentials.
 
• It is useful in predicting the direction of redox reactions.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Zinc and Lead**
 
 
• Zinc is used for galvanizing iron, making alloys, and in batteries.
 
• Lead is used in batteries, radiation shielding, and in some types of glass.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles possesses their own DNA and can synthesise protein for their functions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chloroplast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chloroplasts** are organelles found in plant cells and eukaryotic algae that conduct photosynthesis.
 
• They have their own **DNA and ribosomes**, similar to mitochondria, which allows them to synthesize proteins independently.
 
• The DNA present in chloroplasts is **circular** and resembles the DNA of prokaryotes.
 
• Chloroplasts are known for containing the pigment **chlorophyll**, which is essential for capturing light energy.
 
• They play a crucial role in converting light energy into chemical energy through the process of **photosynthesis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory**

 
 
• This theory suggests that chloroplasts and mitochondria were once free-living prokaryotes.
 
• They were engulfed by a host cell and developed a symbiotic relationship.
 
• This theory is supported by the presence of their own DNA and double membranes.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis Process**
 
 
• Photosynthesis occurs in two stages: the light-dependent reactions and the Calvin cycle.
 
• In the light-dependent reactions, energy from light is used to produce ATP and NADPH.
 
• In the Calvin cycle, ATP and NADPH are used to convert carbon dioxide into glucose.
 
 
 
• **Structure of Chloroplast**
 
 
• Chloroplasts have an outer membrane, an inner membrane, and a thylakoid membrane system.
 
• The thylakoid membranes contain chlorophyll and are the site of the light-dependent reactions.
 
• The stroma is the fluid-filled space surrounding the thylakoids where the Calvin cycle takes place.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Engineering**
 
 
• Chloroplast DNA can be used in genetic engineering to introduce new traits in plants.
 
• Transgenic plants with modified chloroplast genomes can produce biofuels, pharmaceuticals, and other valuable products.
 
• Research in this area is ongoing to enhance the efficiency of photosynthesis and crop yields.

questions.question: Who among the following is/was a famous proponent of Bharatanatyam?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• **Rukmini Devi Arundale** was a renowned Indian classical dancer and choreographer of the Bharatanatyam style of dance.

questions.question: In the Great Stupa at Sanchi there are _______ gateways known as 'Toranas' at the cardinal points to the compass.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Stupa at Sanchi is one of the oldest stone structures in India and an important Buddhist monument.
 
• It was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• The stupa has four elaborately carved gateways known as 'Toranas' at the cardinal points of the compass.
 
• These gateways are intricately decorated with sculptures depicting various events of the Buddha's life and Jataka tales.
 
• The Toranas symbolize the entrance to a sacred space and are significant in Buddhist architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Emperor Ashoka:**

 
 
• A major patron of Buddhism, Ashoka played a critical role in the spread of Buddhism across Asia.
 
• He erected numerous stupas and pillars inscribed with Buddhist teachings and edicts.
 
 
 
• **Stupa:**
 
 
• A stupa is a dome-shaped structure erected as a Buddhist shrine.
 
• It typically contains relics of the Buddha or other holy figures and serves as a place of meditation.
 
 
 
• **Jataka Tales:**
 
 
• These are a voluminous body of literature native to India concerning the previous births of Gautama Buddha in both human and animal form.
 
• The tales are used to convey moral lessons and are important in Buddhist teaching.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist Architecture:**
 
 
• Buddhist architecture includes various structures such as stupas, viharas (monasteries), chaityas (prayer halls), and temples.
 
• These structures are designed to support the practice and teachings of Buddhism.

questions.question: 'Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections' comes under which Article of Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 46**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 46 of the Indian Constitution mandates the promotion of the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and other weaker sections.
 
• This article is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government.
 
• Article 46 aims to protect these communities from social injustice and all forms of exploitation.
 
• The state is encouraged to take special care to promote their educational and economic development.
 
• It highlights the importance of equal opportunities and upliftment of marginalized communities in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• These principles are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• DPSP aims to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They act as guidelines for the central and state governments in India to frame laws and policies.
 
• Though non-justiciable, DPSPs are fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to establish a welfare state.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST)**
 
 
• These are officially designated groups of historically disadvantaged people in India.
 
• SCs and STs have been provided with certain privileges and reservations in educational institutions and government jobs to promote their development.
 
• The Constitution of India recognizes the need for affirmative action to uplift these communities.
 
 
 
• **Social Justice**
 
 
• Social justice refers to the fair and just relation between the individual and society.
 
• It includes the distribution of wealth, opportunities, and privileges within a society.
 
• The aim is to create a society based on equality and solidarity, where human rights are recognized and protected.
 
 
 
• **Educational and Economic Development**
 
 
• Educational development involves providing access to quality education for all, especially marginalized groups.
 
• Economic development includes measures to improve the economic conditions of weaker sections through employment, entrepreneurship, and financial inclusion.
 
• Both aspects are crucial for the holistic development of individuals and communities.

questions.question: Who among the following has written 'Gita Govinda', a Sanskrit epic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jayadeva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gita Govinda** is a renowned 12th-century Sanskrit epic written by the poet **Jayadeva**.
 
• Jayadeva was a celebrated poet during the reign of King **Lakshmanasena** in Bengal.
 
• The epic primarily revolves around the divine love of **Krishna** and the gopis (milkmaids) of Vrindavan, particularly focusing on Krishna's relationship with **Radha**.
 
• Gita Govinda has been highly influential in the **Bhakti movement** and has inspired numerous literary and artistic works in Indian culture.
 
• It is composed of twelve chapters, further divided into twenty-four divisions called **prabandhas**, which contain the songs and hymns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jayadeva**

 
 
• Jayadeva was not only a poet but also a **devotee of Krishna** and his works reflect his deep spiritual connection and devotion.
 
• He is credited with the development of the **Ashtapadi** form, a lyrical poetry format used in the Gita Govinda.
 
 
 
• **Bhakti Movement**
 
 
• The Bhakti movement was a **spiritual resurgence** in India that emphasized personal devotion to deities like Krishna and Rama.
 
• It spanned from the 7th century to the 17th century and had a profound impact on the religious and social fabric of India.
 
 
 
• **Radha-Krishna**
 
 
• Radha and Krishna are central figures in Hinduism and symbolize the epitome of divine love and devotion.
 
• Their story has been a subject of numerous literary, artistic, and devotional works over the centuries.
 
 
 
• **Prabandhas**
 
 
• In the context of Gita Govinda, prabandhas refer to the sections that contain the lyrical compositions and are a significant literary form in Sanskrit literature.
 
• Each prabandha in Gita Govinda is composed of a couple of verses that set the scene followed by a song or hymn.

questions.question: Who were the first foreign rulers of northwest India in the post-Mauryan period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bactrian Greek**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bactrian Greeks were the first foreign rulers to establish control over northwest India following the decline of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• They were part of the Indo-Greek Kingdom, which was formed around 180 BCE after the Greco-Bactrian King Demetrius invaded India.
 
• The Indo-Greek Kingdom extended its influence over parts of modern-day Afghanistan, Pakistan, and northwestern India.
 
• The period of Indo-Greek rule is noted for the introduction of Hellenistic culture, art, and coinage in the region.
 
• The most renowned Indo-Greek ruler was Menander I (Milinda), who is celebrated for his dialogues with the Buddhist sage Nagasena, recorded in the Milinda Panha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-Greek Kingdom**

 
 
• The Indo-Greek Kingdom was established following the fragmentation of the Greco-Bactrian Kingdom, located in present-day Afghanistan and Central Asia.
 
• It is known for its fusion of Greek and Indian cultures, particularly in art and architecture.
 
• The kingdom played a significant role in the spread of Buddhism in Central Asia and India.
 
• Indo-Greek coinage is renowned for its artistic quality and bilingual inscriptions in Greek and Prakrit.
 
 
 
• **Menander I (Milinda)**
 
 
• Menander I was one of the most prominent Indo-Greek kings, who ruled from approximately 165 to 130 BCE.
 
• He is best known for his discussions on Buddhism with the sage Nagasena, which are recorded in the text "Milinda Panha" (The Questions of King Milinda).
 
• Menander's reign marked the zenith of the Indo-Greek influence in the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Greco-Bactrian Kingdom**
 
 
• The Greco-Bactrian Kingdom was established around 256 BCE, following the fragmentation of Alexander the Great's empire.
 
• It was located in Bactria, present-day Afghanistan and parts of Central Asia.
 
• The kingdom is known for its rich cultural heritage and contributions to the spread of Hellenistic culture in Asia.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Mauryan Empire**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire began to decline after the death of Emperor Ashoka around 232 BCE.
 
• Internal conflicts and succession disputes weakened the central authority, leading to the fragmentation of the empire.
 
• The decline of the Mauryan Empire created a power vacuum that facilitated the emergence of foreign rulers like the Indo-Greeks in northwest India.

questions.question: As of 2023, what is the number of major public seaports in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India has a total of **12 major public seaports** as of 2023.
 
• These major ports are governed by the central government and fall under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.
 
• The major ports facilitate a significant portion of India's trade and are critical to the country's economy.
 
• Examples of major ports include Mumbai Port, Chennai Port, and Kolkata Port.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Port Infrastructure**

 
 
• Ports are essential for the maritime trade and logistics sector, supporting the import and export of goods.
 
• Major ports are equipped with advanced cargo handling facilities, warehouses, and connectivity to rail and road networks.
 
 
 
• **Port Trusts**
 
 
• Each major port in India is managed by a Port Trust, which is a statutory body under the Major Port Trusts Act of 1963.
 
• The Port Trusts ensure the efficient operation and development of the ports.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance**
 
 
• Major ports handle approximately 60% of India's total cargo traffic.
 
• They play a crucial role in the economic growth by facilitating international trade and commerce.
 
 
 
• **Recent Developments**
 
 
• The Indian government has been focusing on modernizing port infrastructure through the Sagarmala project.
 
• This project aims to enhance port connectivity and promote port-led development in coastal regions.

questions.question: In cycling, what is a 'peloton'?

options.text: The finish line of a race
A cycling technique for climbing hills
A group of riders in a tight pack during a race
The starting line of a race

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A group of riders in a tight pack during a race**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term "peloton" is derived from French, meaning "platoon" or "group." It refers to a large group of cyclists riding closely together during a race.
 
• The main advantage of riding in a peloton is to reduce air resistance, allowing riders to conserve energy by drafting off one another.
 
• Riders in the peloton take turns at the front to distribute the workload evenly among them.
 
• The peloton can significantly influence the dynamics and strategies of a race, including the pace and formation of breakaways.
 
• It is a common sight in road racing events like the Tour de France, where teamwork and strategy play crucial roles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drafting**

 
 
• Drafting is a technique where cyclists ride closely behind one another to benefit from reduced wind resistance.
 
• This technique is crucial in a peloton as it helps riders conserve energy and maintain higher speeds.
 
 
 
• **Breakaway**
 
 
• A breakaway occurs when one or more riders accelerate ahead of the peloton, attempting to gain a significant lead.
 
• Breakaways require strategic timing and immense effort to succeed, often involving cooperation among the escaping riders.
 
 
 
• **Domestique**
 
 
• A domestique is a rider who works for the benefit of their team leader, often sacrificing their own chances of winning.
 
• Domestiques play crucial roles in protecting the leader from wind, fetching supplies, and controlling the pace of the peloton.
 
 
 
• **Team Strategy**
 
 
• Teams in cycling races employ various strategies such as controlling the peloton, forming breakaways, and setting up lead-outs for sprint finishes.
 
• Effective team strategy can be the deciding factor in the success of individual riders and the team as a whole.
 
 
 
• **Tour de France**
 
 
• The Tour de France is one of the most prestigious and challenging cycling races in the world.
 
• It consists of multiple stages over a span of three weeks, covering various terrains including mountains and flat roads.
 
• Riding in the peloton is a common sight during the Tour, where teamwork and endurance are paramount.

questions.question: Which author wrote the Hindi novel 'Tamas'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhisham Sahani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bhisham Sahani is the author of the renowned Hindi novel **'Tamas'**.
 
• 'Tamas' is a significant work in Hindi literature that deals with the horrors of the Partition of India in 1947.
 
• The novel was first published in **1974** and received critical acclaim for its realistic portrayal of communal violence.
 
• Bhisham Sahani was awarded the prestigious **Sahitya Akademi Award** in 1975 for 'Tamas'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhisham Sahani**

 
 
• Born on 8 August 1915 in Rawalpindi, Bhisham Sahani was a notable writer, playwright, and actor.
 
• He was a recipient of the **Padma Bhushan** in 1998 for his contributions to Indian literature and arts.
 
• Other notable works by Bhisham Sahani include 'Madhavi', 'Basanti', and 'Kaddi Aur Mitti'.
 
• He was actively involved in the Indian People’s Theatre Association (IPTA) and contributed significantly to theatre and cinema.
 
 
 
• **'Tamas' Adaptations**
 
 
• 'Tamas' was adapted into a critically acclaimed television series in 1987, directed by Govind Nihalani.
 
• The TV series featured prominent actors like Om Puri, Deepa Sahi, and Amrish Puri, and won several awards for its impactful storytelling.
 
• The adaptation helped bring the novel's themes and historical context to a wider audience.
 
 
 
• **Partition of India**
 
 
• The Partition of India in 1947 led to the creation of two independent dominions, India and Pakistan.
 
• This event resulted in one of the largest mass migrations in human history, with an estimated 10-15 million people displaced.
 
• The partition was marked by large-scale communal violence, with significant loss of life and property.

questions.question: As of July 2023, 137 unique products under 'One District, One Product' scheme has been notified from how many districts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**713**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As of July 2023, the 'One District, One Product' (ODOP) scheme has notified 137 unique products from 713 districts in India.
 
• The ODOP scheme aims to promote local products and crafts specific to each district to boost economic growth and employment.
 
• ODOP products range from agricultural produce, handicrafts, handlooms, and processed food items, representing the unique strengths of each district.
 
• The initiative is part of the broader vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-reliant India) to make Indian products globally competitive.
 
• ODOP also focuses on building robust supply chains, better packaging, marketing, and branding of these district-specific products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan**

 
 
• Launched by PM Narendra Modi in May 2020 to make India self-reliant.
 
• Aims to support local manufacturing, improve the supply chain, and reduce dependency on imports.
 
• Focuses on five pillars: economy, infrastructure, system, demography, and demand.
 
 
 
• **Districts as Export Hubs**
 
 
• In line with ODOP, the Indian government has identified districts with export potential to boost local economies.
 
• Efforts are made to provide necessary infrastructure, logistics, and market access to these districts.
 
• The initiative aims to create a district-wise export strategy to promote local products globally.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Indications (GI)**
 
 
• A GI tag is used on products that have a specific geographical origin and possess qualities or reputation inherent to that location.
 
• Many ODOP products are also GI-tagged, enhancing their marketability and authenticity.
 
• Examples include Darjeeling Tea, Madhubani Paintings, and Kanchipuram Silk.
 
 
 
• **Cluster-Based Development**
 
 
• ODOP focuses on cluster-based development to enhance the production capacity and competitiveness of local industries.
 
• Clusters help in achieving economies of scale, better resource management, and collective marketing efforts.

questions.question: What is the height of the Kanchenjunga peak of Himalaya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8598 metres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kanchenjunga is the third highest mountain in the world, located in the Himalayas.
 
• The height of Kanchenjunga is 8598 metres (28,169 feet).
 
• Kanchenjunga is situated on the border between Nepal and the Indian state of Sikkim.
 
• Kanchenjunga has five main peaks, and its name translates to "The Five Treasures of Snows."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayas:**

 
 
• The Himalayas are a mountain range in Asia, separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• They include over fifty mountains exceeding 7,200 metres (23,600 feet) in elevation, including the world's highest peak, Mount Everest.
 
• The range has a profound effect on the climate of the region, influencing the monsoon and acting as a barrier to cold winds from the north.
 
 
 
• **Mount Everest:**
 
 
• Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world, standing at 8,848 metres (29,029 feet).
 
• It is located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas and lies on the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Nepal:**
 
 
• Nepal is a landlocked country in South Asia, sharing borders with China and India.
 
• The country is known for its diverse geography, including fertile plains, subalpine forests, and eight of the world's ten tallest mountains.
 
 
 
• **Sikkim:**
 
 
• Sikkim is a state in northeastern India, bordered by Bhutan, Tibet, and Nepal.
 
• It is known for its mountainous terrain and is home to Kanchenjunga, the highest peak in India.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Census Act enacted and extended to the whole of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1948**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Census Act of India was enacted in the year **1948**.
 
• The Act provides the legal framework for conducting the decennial census in India.
 
• It was extended to the whole of India and applies to every state and union territory.
 
• The Act empowers the government to collect demographic data about the population.
 
• The first census after the enactment of the Act was conducted in 1951.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census Definition**

 
 
• A census is a systematic enumeration of the population, typically recording various details of individuals.
 
• It is conducted at regular intervals, usually every ten years.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Census**
 
 
• Provides essential data for policymaking and planning.
 
• Helps in the allocation of government resources and services.
 
• Assists in electoral boundary delimitation and representation.
 
 
 
• **History of Census in India**
 
 
• The first synchronous census in India was conducted in 1881.
 
• Since then, censuses have been conducted every ten years without interruption.
 
 
 
• **Modern Census Techniques**
 
 
• Use of technology such as mobile apps and digital data collection.
 
• Incorporation of geographic information systems (GIS) for accurate mapping.

questions.question: What is the usual treatment on repo rates by the Reserve Bank of India in case of a hawkish monetary policy stance?

options.text: Reduced sharply by more than 100 bps

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increased**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a hawkish monetary policy stance, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) aims to control inflation by increasing the repo rate.
 
• Increasing the repo rate makes borrowing more expensive for commercial banks, which in turn reduces the money supply in the economy.
 
• This action helps to curb inflationary pressures by discouraging excessive spending and investment.
 
• The RBI's decision to increase the repo rate is a signal to the market about its intent to tighten monetary conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Repo Rate:**

 
 
• It is the rate at which the central bank of a country (RBI in India) lends money to commercial banks in case of any shortfall of funds.
 
• It is used by monetary authorities to control inflation.
 
 
 
• **Hawkish Monetary Policy:**
 
 
• It refers to the approach taken by a central bank to increase interest rates to keep inflation in check.
 
• This stance is typically adopted when the economy is growing quickly and inflation is rising.
 
 
 
• **Inflation:**
 
 
• It is the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services is rising, and subsequently, the purchasing power is falling.
 
• Central banks attempt to limit inflation, and avoid deflation, to keep the economy running smoothly.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy:**
 
 
• It is the process by which the monetary authority of a country controls the supply of money, often targeting an inflation rate or interest rate to ensure price stability and general trust in the currency.
 
• In India, it is managed by the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.question: Who among the following was India's first cricket team captain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CK Nayudu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• CK Nayudu was the first captain of the Indian cricket team in Test matches.
 
• He led the Indian team in their debut Test match against England at Lord's in 1932.
 
• Nayudu was known for his aggressive batting and his ability to hit long sixes, earning him a reputation as a powerful batsman.
 
• He was awarded the Padma Bhushan, India's third-highest civilian award, in 1956 for his contributions to cricket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Early Life and Career**

 
 
• CK Nayudu was born on October 31, 1895, in Nagpur, Maharashtra.
 
• He made his first-class debut in 1916 for the Hindus in the Bombay Quadrangular tournament.
 
 
 
• **Domestic Cricket**
 
 
• He played for several domestic teams, including the Holkar team in the Ranji Trophy.
 
• Nayudu captained Holkar to several Ranji Trophy titles, establishing himself as a dominant force in Indian domestic cricket.
 
 
 
• **Legacy**
 
 
• CK Nayudu's leadership and prowess on the field laid the foundation for future generations of Indian cricketers.
 
• The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) instituted the CK Nayudu Lifetime Achievement Award in his honor, recognizing outstanding contributions to Indian cricket.
 
 
 
• **Post-Retirement**
 
 
• After retiring from cricket, Nayudu continued to be involved in the sport as a selector and mentor for younger players.
 
• His contributions to cricket were celebrated throughout his life, and he remains a respected figure in Indian cricket history.

questions.question: Which social reformer from South India founded the Self Respect Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**EV Ramaswamy Naicker**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **EV Ramaswamy Naicker**, also known as Periyar, was a prominent social reformer from South India.
 
• He founded the **Self Respect Movement** in 1925 to promote social equality and fight against caste discrimination.
 
• The movement aimed to instill a sense of pride and dignity among the oppressed classes, challenging the existing social norms and practices.
 
• Periyar was a staunch advocate for women's rights and worked tirelessly for the eradication of untouchability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self Respect Movement**

 
 
• Launched in Tamil Nadu, this movement sought to achieve a society where backward castes have equal human rights, and encouraging them to have self-respect.
 
• It played a crucial role in promoting rationalism and anti-Brahminism.
 
• The movement opposed the concept of the superiority of Brahmins and other upper castes.
 
• It also worked towards the upliftment of women and advocated for their education and equal rights.
 
 
 
• **Periyar's Legacy**
 
 
• Periyar's ideas and principles continue to influence many social and political movements in Tamil Nadu and other parts of India.
 
• He is regarded as the father of the Dravidian movement.
 
• His works have been translated into several languages and continue to inspire activists fighting for social justice.
 
 
 
• **Rationalism**
 
 
• Rationalism is the practice or principle of basing opinions and actions on reason and knowledge rather than on religious belief or emotional response.
 
• Periyar advocated for rationalism, rejecting religious dogmas and superstitions.
 
• He believed that rational thinking was essential for social progress and equality.
 
 
 
• **Anti-Caste Movements in India**
 
 
• Anti-caste movements have a long history in India, aimed at eradicating the caste system and promoting social equality.
 
• Other notable leaders of anti-caste movements include Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and Jyotirao Phule.
 
• These movements have significantly contributed to the socio-political fabric of India, advocating for the rights of the oppressed and marginalized communities.
